text:
alex: Heads-up — hit a weird typing regression in the JS SDK when running our sample on the edge runtime. Generics collapse to `any` after bundling with esbuild + tsconfig set to `module: 'ESNext'` + `esModuleInterop: true`. Anyone seen this?

sam: Hmm. Are you using `skipLibCheck`? That often hides underlying mismatch between declaration shapes.

alex: yep `skipLibCheck: true` in the sample's tsconfig to speed CI. If I disable it, I get a ton of errors inside `@redwood/inference` overloads. But the runtime still works; it's just the types that are wrong — callers lose generic inference.

carla: This sounds like the overload resolution + `unknown`/`any` flip. We had a previous patch where one overload returned `Promise<T>` and a fallback returned `Promise<any>` which made TS pick the weaker signature after bundling. Do you have an example?

alex: Minimal repro in the sample:

```ts
// calling code
const client = new Client();
const r = await client.generate<string>({ model: 'redwood-small', prompt: 'x' });
// expected r to be string, but inferred as any after build
```

and inside node_modules types there are overloads like:

```ts
generate<T>(opts: GenerateOptions & { responseType: 'raw' }): Promise<T>
generate(opts: GenerateOptions & { responseType?: undefined }): Promise<any>
```

carla: Yeah that's the culprit — the second overload widens to `any`. TS chooses the less specific signature when it can't safely unify across module boundaries.

jordyn: Another angle: ESM/CJS interop changes the shape of the imported types in some bundlers. With `esModuleInterop` you might end up referencing `default` vs named which can pick a different entrypoint `.d.ts` depending on resolution. Did the sample bundle create a flat single file or keep node_modules types?

alex: esbuild produced a single bundle for the edge sample. Types are still being checked by tsc separately in CI. The bundle makes runtime fine, tsc complains/infers wrong.

sam: Try making the overloads more explicit so inference doesn't fall back to `any`. e.g. add a generic fallback overload: `generate<T = any>(opts: GenerateOptions & { responseType?: undefined }): Promise<T>` — forces callers to get `T` even for the fallback. Ugly but pragmatic.

carla: Another approach: prefer `unknown` instead of `any` in the fallback and then narrow inside implementation. If an overload returns `Promise<unknown>` the compiler won't implicitly widen to `any` in some cases. Also export a typed helper `asString` for common shapes.

jordyn: We should also audit tsconfigs across samples: `moduleResolution`, `module`, `target`, `esModuleInterop`, and `allowSyntheticDefaultImports` must be consistent. Edge runtime sample should use `module: 'ESNext'` + `moduleResolution: 'bundler'` for esbuild, while node samples use `node16`/`nodenext`. Mismatch causes type resolution drift.

ci-bot: CI failed for sample-edge: types check error in `/samples/edge-ts/src/index.ts:12` — "Type 'any' is not assignable to type 'string'". See job: https://ci.internal/3456

alex: Thanks — I'll try the explicit fallback overload and flip `any` -> `unknown` in the SDK types, run the sample matrix, and update the sample tsconfig to match bundler resolution.

sam: If you want I can open a tiny PR that adds a `types.md` note in samples explaining which tsconfigs to use per runtime (edge vs node). Saves others the confusion.

carla: +1. Also let's add a unit test that asserts `generate<string>(...)` is inferred as `string` (tsd or dtslint) so we catch regressions in CI.

alex: Great plan. I'll push a branch with the overload tweak + tsconfig harmonization and tag you both. Will also disable `skipLibCheck` in the edge sample CI for now so we don't silently accept drift.

jordyn: FYI we should avoid changing public typing shapes without a migration note. If we change fallback `any`->`unknown` it might surface new type errors to customers. Let's include a short changelog entry in the SDK release notes.

alex: Good call. I'll include that. Thanks all :thumbsup:
